dependencies.basis: TurkStat's national accounts (including the ESA 2010 / SNA 2008 series) are compiled following the international guidelines of SNA 2008 and ESA 2010 for GDP calculation by production, expenditure and income approaches, supply-use balancing, and regional accounts. Evidence: "The international guidelines applied in the calculation of GDP are ESA 2010 and SNA 2008. ... The most recent standards guiding these revisions are the System of National Accounts (2008 SNA) and the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010)."

National Accounts of Turkey (GDP) are produced within TurkStat's System of National Accounts in line with SNA 2008 (and ESA 2010) concepts, definitions and balancing procedures. Evidence: "In Türkiye, estimations related to the National Accounts System are in line with SNA and ESA guidelines. ... The international guidelines applied in the calculation of GDP are ESA 2010 and SNA 2008."

Provincial Gross Regional Domestic Product estimates (including Istanbul) are compiled as regional accounts in accordance with SNA 2008, ESA 2010 and the Regional Accounts Manual, using the same conceptual framework and balancing as national GDP. Evidence: "Regional accounts are compiled in accordance with the System of National Accounts (SNA- 2008) published by the United Nations, the European System of Accounts (ESA-2010) applied in European Union member countries, and the Regional Accounts Manual."

Provincial Gross Regional Domestic Product estimates are compiled as regional accounts in accordance with SNA 2008 and ESA 2010. Türkiye's Balance of Payments statistics are compiled by the CBRT according to the concepts, definitions, classifications and presentation of BPM6. Evidence: "Balance of payments and international investment position statistics are compiled in accordance with the international standards set forth in the “Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, 6th Edition (BPM6)”, which is prepared by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to provide guidance to member countries."

The CPI classification structure has been switched to COICOP-2018 (and weights derived consistently with it) to align with international standards and Eurostat requirements for candidate countries. Evidence: "With the change in the base year, it has been decided to switch from the current classification structure used in the CPI to the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP-2018), which better reflects current consumption patterns. ... The methodology of the CPI is based on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Consumer Price Index Handbook."

In the expenditure approach to GDP, data on exports and imports of services are taken from the CBRT Balance of Payments statistics. Evidence: "Data on exports and imports of goods are sourced from Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat) Foreign Trade Statistics, while data on service exports and imports are obtained from the Central Bank Balance of Payments statistics."

Major source data for goods trade, freight/insurance, international trade in services and short-term trade credits in the BOP are provided by TurkStat foreign-trade and related statistics. Evidence: "The major sources of the balance of payments statistics are; ... Foreign trade statistics compiled by the Turkstat, ... Credit and debit figures on freight and insurance regarding merchandise trade provided by the Turkstat, ... Credit and debit figures on International Trade in Services Statistics provided by the Turkstat, ... Short-term trade credits compiled by the Turkstat using direct reporting method"

National accounts use CBRT BOP data for the services component of exports and imports in the expenditure approach and for consistency checks. Evidence: "Data on exports and imports of goods are sourced from Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat) Foreign Trade Statistics, while data on service exports and imports are obtained from the Central Bank Balance of Payments statistics."

The Central Bank of Iran publishes annual national accounts by activity and institutional sector on the basis of the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008), with base year 1395. Evidence: "حسابهای ملی سالانه ایران به تفکیک بخش‌های فعالیتی و نهادی اقتصاد بر مبنای نظام حسابهای ملی 2008 به قیمت‌ها‌ی جاری و ثابت سال پایه 1395 ... تهیه و تدوین ارقام بر مبنای آخرین نسخه استاندارد نظام حساب‌های ملی 2008 (SNA)"

_dropped.why: [SUSPECT] URL https://dsbb.imf.org/sdds/dqaf-base/country/TUR/category/CPI00 returns HTTP 200, and the exact URL is confirmed as a real, indexed IMF DSBB page for Turkey CPI via WebSearch. However the site is an Angular SPA that loads DQAF text via authenticated/dynamic AJAX calls (api/country/... endpoints requiring POST payloads) -- WebFetch returned only the static shell with no country-specific content, and a Wayback Machine cross-check was blocked by egress policy (archive.org not reachable from this sandbox). Could not directly confirm the quoted sentence 'Moreover Consumer Price Index manual is followed in the CPI.' on this page. The underlying substantive claim (TurkStat CPI methodology based on the IMF CPI framework) IS independently corroborated by a different, fully verified official TurkStat document (see the un-coicop-2018 dependency below, same coicop_download PDF): 'The methodology of the CPI is based on the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Consumer Price Index Handbook.' Given the specific cited page's content could not be directly retrieved, marking SUSPECT rather than VERIFIED despite the strong corroboration of the underlying fact elsewhere.
